chunks: And by this chain, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic:
'So is he who was upon a clear proof from his Lord and a witness from Him follows it' [11:17]

So he said: Amir al-Mu'minin, may God's blessings be upon him, is the witness over the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), and the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) was upon a clear proof from his Lord.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin — Commander/Leader of the Believers, the title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib
key_terms.بَيِّنَة: Clear proof/manifest evidence — refers to the Prophet's direct divine guidance and certainty of faith
key_terms.شَاهِد: Witness — the one who follows and attests; here interpreted as Imam Ali's role as witness to the Prophet's mission
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific for God used throughout hadith literature

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'witness' mentioned in Quran 11:17 according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal asks Imam Abu al-Hasan (likely Imam al-Ridha) about the Quranic verse 11:17, which speaks of one who 'was upon a clear proof from his Lord and a witness from Him follows it.' The Imam explains that Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (peace be upon him) is the 'witness' — the one who follows and attests to the Prophet Muhammad, who himself was 'upon a clear proof from his Lord.' This interpretation situates Ali as a divinely-appointed witness to the Prophethood, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of Imamate as an extension of prophetic authority. The early Muslim community would have understood this as a claim about Ali's unique spiritual station and his role as the authentic continuator of the Prophet's mission.

en.hubeali: And by this chaim, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ahmad Bin Umar Al Hallal who said,
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[11:17] So the one who was upon a clear Proof from his Lord, and a witness from Him recites it.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, is the witness upon Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> upon clear proof from his<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from Mu‘allah ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Ahmad ibn ‘Umar al-Hallal who has said that he asked Imam abu al-Hassan (a.s.)
about the meaning of the following verse of the holy Quran:
“Should they be compared with those whose Lord has given them a guidance which is testified by a witness from among their own people . .” [11:17]
The Imam (a.s.) said, “Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) testified to support the holy Prophet (s.a.) and the holy Prophet received supporting evidence from his Lord.”
